about: The research so far behind a hazard that has no damage curve, in this repository or in Hazard's. One entry per document; 'asset' is an asset slug or '*' for every asset; 'finding' is the document's own conclusion, kept short and quoted or closely paraphrased from it. The build checks every path and links it where it is (Damage: this repository; Hazard: its main, else the branch that holds it). 'branch' names the Hazard branch that holds the content when main has a different version of the file.

entries.title: Damage's scope: a damage curve prices physical destruction only
entries.finding: Heat is treated as changing how an asset performs (derating, ageing), which sits outside a damage curve; disruption and derating are a separate stage.

entries.title: BESS heat: physical effects and first-screen feasibility (Hazard, 21 Oct 2026)
entries.finding: Heat can cause lasting physical harm to batteries (an EPRI field case, LFP lab studies), but the reviewed sources do not yet support an outdoor-temperature-to-repair-cost curve for the reference plant.

entries.title: Heat: define the consequence before building the model (Hazard, 21 Oct 2026)
entries.finding: Parked by the owner on 21 Oct: temporary derating, permanent ageing and acute failure need separate definitions, and working cooling should be compared with impaired cooling. No owner ruling yet.

entries.title: Hail × wind farm: the no-go decision (docs r2)
entries.finding: "No candidate exposes a source-native fractional economic endpoint comparable to the cell's y-axis": every source stops before repair cost, so no curve ships.

entries.title: Hail × wind farm: evidence search, second pass (cut-off 29 Jul 2026)
entries.finding: 24 sources registered across DOE/OSTI, NREL, Sandia, NOAA, IEC, DNV and theses; of 73 NOAA turbine reports, the only one typed as hail was a 1995 rooftop turbine blown off by winds.

entries.title: Hail × wind farm: evidence search, first pass (cut-off 28 Jul 2026)
entries.finding: Lab tests, simulations and erosion models were found; none links a hail event to a blade's repair cost.

entries.title: Hail × wind farm: why the old curve was rejected
entries.finding: The legacy wind-turbine hail curve is a buildings-and-cars hail curve relabelled for wind, with a centimetre/inch unit error.

entries.title: Hazard × asset coverage plan: decisions D-004, D-006, D-012
entries.finding: Hail × wind farm was reopened first, closed as a zero-curve v0.1 placeholder, and kept so after the deeper review. It reopens only on paired blade inspections with repair costs, a final ISO 19392-7 hail standard, or an owner-approved expert-judgment curve.

entries.title: Hail × wind farm: what Hazard must do (handoff)
entries.finding: Fail closed with no runtime curve; do not reuse solar, erosion or legacy real-estate curves.

entries.title: Substation: which existing curves could be reused (16 Oct 2026)
entries.finding: Only the curves already in this repository were checked; no outside search was run. "No station response found in this reviewed current/proposed inventory. Missing evidence is not proof of zero station damage."

entries.title: Substation damage plan: decision SD-D12
entries.finding: Hail is a recorded gap: missing coverage is never zero.

entries.title: Hazard's substation decisions: DD-SUB26 (17 Oct 2026)
entries.finding: Owner decision: hail is an explicit scope exclusion for this delivery, not a negligible-risk claim or a numerical zero; revisit only if scope or evidence changes.

entries.title: Hazard's substation reference profile: the hail research lead
entries.finding: Hail is flagged as a bounded research lead ("do not infer zero risk or borrow PV fragility"); that research has not been done.

entries.title: Hazard's battery decisions: DD-BESS25 (20 Oct 2026)
entries.finding: Owner direction: defer strong wind, tornado and the other additional hazards. "This is a scope direction, not a finding that omitted hazards are negligible or have zero loss."

entries.title: Hazard's battery multi-hazard roadmap
entries.finding: Hail: "Deferred; outside the completed first pass." Deferred does not mean negligible, safe or zero loss.

entries.title: Battery hail: the field-report register
entries.finding: Not searched for any part: nobody has looked for field reports yet. This is the default, not a finding.

entries.title: Does it happen? Leads from the battery's design (hail row)
entries.finding: Design leads only (panel denting, condenser coils, both rated low); the recommended next step, "search first; park if nothing", has not been run.

entries.title: Hazard's battery decisions: DD-BESS25 (20 Oct 2026)
entries.finding: Owner direction: defer strong wind and tornado after the first pass. A scope direction, not a finding of zero loss.

entries.title: Hazard's battery multi-hazard roadmap (step 4)
entries.finding: Convective wind was in the planned sequence, then deferred by owner direction; no qualification or execution now.

entries.title: Battery hurricane wind cell: its scope
entries.finding: Treats convective wind and tornado as a separate scope from the hurricane wind curve.

entries.title: Battery convective wind: the field-report register
entries.finding: Not searched: nobody has looked for field reports yet.

entries.title: Does it happen? Leads from the battery's design (heat row, 19 Oct 2026)
entries.finding: Heat is the strongest design lead (ageing doubles per +10 °C, chiller and converter derating) but works through performance: "Performance, not damage — no curve." No field evidence was searched.
